transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I came in because... I just feel completely flat inside lately. Even when my children come over to sit with me, or the sun is shining right on my garden out back—things that usually make me smile—I don't feel anything at all. It's like the part of me that could be glad or comforted just shut off.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
It's been about two weeks now. Ever since my husband collapsed. The paramedics, they had to work on him right there in our kitchen... and I suppose that's when this all started.
Since that day, do unwanted memories or images of your husband collapsing keep popping into your mind?

No, doctor, I... I haven't really had that. I don't keep seeing it happen in my head, if that's what you mean. 

It's really just that... that blank feeling I mentioned. I haven't noticed any memories or pictures of it popping up like that.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life, or is this the first time?

No, doctor. This is the first time. I mean, I'm 81 years old, so I've certainly been through difficult things in my life before, but... I've never had a time where I just stopped feeling altogether. It's completely new to me.
How has your sleep been over these past two weeks?

My sleep? Oh, it's... well, it hasn't really changed much. I sleep about the same as I always have. I haven't noticed any real trouble falling asleep or anything like that. It's just... I just wake up and still have that same empty feeling. But the sleeping part itself is fine.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or eating habits over these past two weeks?

Not really, no. My appetite is pretty much the same as it's always been. I still eat my regular meals... I mean, I guess I just eat because I know it's time to eat, but I haven't noticed any real changes in how much I'm eating or anything like that. It's just normal, I suppose.
Have you noticed any change in your energy levels, or have you been feeling unusually tired or fatigued over these past two weeks?

No, my energy is about the same. I don't feel any more tired than usual. I still have the energy to do my daily routine around the house, it's just... I just do it without really feeling anything about it. But physically, no, I haven't been unusually fatigued.
Have you been feeling guilty or blaming yourself for what happened to your husband?

Guilty? No, I wouldn't say that. I don't blame myself for what happened to him. It was... well, it was just one of those terrible things that happen. I know I couldn't have stopped it. I just miss him, but I don't feel like it was my fault.
Over these past two weeks, have you had any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or thoughts of wanting to die?

No, no thoughts like that. I mean, I'm grieving and it's hard without him, but I don't want to die. I haven't been thinking that life isn't worth living or anything of that sort. I just... I just want to get through each day. But no, no thoughts of hurting myself or wanting to end it.
